lines: A split seam can ruin a journey faster than a bad map.
I once made boots that outlasted three owners and four <wavy>bad roads</wavy>.
My apron has seen enough mistakes to deserve its own corner by the fire.
There is a story from the cauldron, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Once a boot came in with more mud than leather and still demanded dignity.
A traveler brought me a saddle so worn it looked relieved to stop moving.
I stitched through a storm once while the roof tested every bucket we owned.
A child made a pouch for pebbles and called it treasure storage. Fair enough.
The old apron has saved me from stains, sparks, and one very angry dye pot.
I once repaired a strap five minutes before it would have ruined a journey.
A villager claimed their boots shrank. The mud told another story.
There was a week when everyone needed belts at once. Nobody explained it.
A dye batch went wrong and the whole village learned a new shade of regret.
I made gloves for winter and got paid in soup. Good bargain.
A saddle squeaked so loudly the horse looked embarrassed.
I once found a lost emerald in a torn pouch and returned both with advice.
Rain taught me my first real lesson about lazy stitching.
A cloak I patched came back from a raid with ash and gratitude on it.
The tannery door sticks every spring like it has opinions about humidity.
